target.name: RobCo
target.founder: Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt, Constantin Dresel

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $160M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
RobCo is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt, and Constantin Dresel, having raised $160M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers (including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $160M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $320M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer set skews toward later-stage valuations given three of four comparables are Series B companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $272M to $2.0B, with a median of $1.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material stage and timing differences within the peer set—particularly the presence of Series B comparables valued substantially above RobCo's current funding level. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the stage-progression multiplier given market conditions at RobCo's next capital event, and the relevance of Series B peer valuations to a Series A company absent comparable revenue or deployment metrics.
